answer: Each identity declares one domain on the meadow board and locks a 75-credit domain bond. Work must carry that tag, and sonnet auditors recompute tags from the ledger; out-of-domain credit is rejected and the bond frozen. The k-th fake locks its own 75 credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 75,000. An identity that tries to wander into a second domain forfeits standing and posts a fresh 75-credit bond, so rented standing cannot cross domains. Domain-hopping rings fail: tags are key-bound, switching resets standing. An honest identity declares once and reclaims its bond after a clean epoch.
